rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "at the core stands the database schema ... after we design the schema we lock it in so the coding agents have to fall into compliance"
rule.text: The schema folders (schema/cortex, schema/workspace, engines/<engine>/schema) are the database. Code reads and writes the tables they declare, with the columns they declare, and nothing else; it never creates, alters or drops a table, a column, an index or a constraint, and never works out at run time what a file declares. A table, a column or a value the schema has no place for is a stop, not a workaround.
rule.breach: the store, which creates a file only from the schema folders and refuses a file whose tables differ from them; the spec check over the schema folders; review

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "its both referential integrity and data consistency preventing drift"
rule.text: Every reference between rows is a foreign key, every value is constrained by its type and its checks (STRICT tables), every rule a foreign key cannot state is a query of an integrity.sql, and the store runs them all on every write: foreign keys on, the integrity queries before every commit. Nothing is checked by convention alone, and no code turns a check off.
rule.breach: the store's tests, which plant a row breaking each constraint and each integrity query and prove the commit is refused; review

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "a cortex schema global and schema per engine"; docs/engines.md
rule.text: What every engine shares is the cortex's; what is one engine's alone is that engine's, in its own tables in its own crate, named <engine>__<name>. Shared code (the model, the interface, the store, the server, the canvas) never names an engine, an engine table or an engine column; an engine never writes a cortex table's rows but through the interface, and never another engine's.
rule.breach: the architecture check (a database named outside its engine); the spec check (an engine table outside its engine's folder, or named without its prefix); the kit

rule.from: docs/engines.md; the MySQL engine as merged
rule.text: A schema written into the store and read back is the same schema: every part, every value, every order. What the model does not describe is kept exactly as written and written back in its place. Nothing is dropped, truncated, defaulted or summarised on the way in or out.
rule.breach: the kit's round trip of every sample through an engine's tables; the store's round trip of every sample of every engine

rule.text: The log (turns, operations, row_changes, value_changes, versions) is appended to and never updated or deleted, but a turn's state and its verdict; a change to the current model is written in the same transaction as the operation that records it, with every row and value it changed.

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-23: "this is not acceptable and create a harness to stop you"
rule.text: Shared code shows what an engine declares and never assumes one: no engine's connection field, kind, option, table or column is named in it. Every test of shared code runs on every engine of the test registry, and Quill, built unlike MySQL on purpose, is one of them; what each engine is tested on is data.
rule.breach: the architecture check; the tests of shared code, run on every engine

rule.text: One session, one agent, sequential: the agent that holds a task does every step itself. It never spawns, delegates to or messages another agent, subagent or session, and never asks another model to build or verify a part.
rule.breach: the build session's settings, which deny the tools that spawn or message another agent; review of the PR's history

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "standards once abandoned it is impossible to troubleshoot; one fix will break 10 others"
rule.text: A task file lists under agent-decides the only things its agent decides: the names and the decomposition of private code inside the files it owns, the standard means of a step, the contents of its fixtures within the cases listed, its commit granularity. Everything else is written in the task file, the root, these rules, the schema folders or the merged code; a build that decides anything else is closed, and the step it departed from is named in the review.
rule.breach: review of the PR against the task file

rule.text: No commit, branch, PR, file or comment carries an attribution to a coding agent or a model: no co-author line, no generated-by line, no trailer. The work is the operator's.
rule.breach: the build session's settings (attribution off); review

rule.text: tools/check.sh is the one command every change passes, the same locally and in CI: formatting, lint, every test (the kit, the architecture check and the spec check among them). Nothing is done until it passes; its last line is in the PR.
rule.breach: CI; the gates of every task

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24, after the methodology of the Gryphon Knowledge Network
rule.text: A build starts with a model pointed at one task file, specs/tasks/<file>.xml, as the first message of a new session on a checkout of the head of main updated from origin; nothing else is said. A session that holds anything before that line beyond what the harness gives every session (its own text, CLAUDE.md, its settings) stops, says so and builds nothing. The task file's start element names the branch, the PR title and the read order; the agent writes its own label.
rule.breach: review of the branch name, the PR title and the PR body's statement of the session

rule.text: Every rule here binds every task, whether or not a gate of the task names it.
